Last month, OpenAI teased a hardware product under the Codex brand. Today, the company officially unveiled the result of its collaboration with Work Louder: a Codex Micro keyboard priced at US$230.

Here's the product introduction:

The keyboard comes in two versions: a clicky (tactile) version and a silent version.

According to the website: "Every Agent key lights up with different RGB effects based on Codex's real-time status, so you can tell at a glance who's thinking, running, waiting, or done before switching conversations."

The product page also lists three Codex-exclusive features:

  • Instant trigger skills: flick the joystick to launch commonly used Codex workflows, such as reviewing a PR (pull request), debugging, or refactoring code.
  • Centralise your core actions: command keys give you dedicated shortcuts for your most-used operations, including accept, reject, push-to-talk, start a new conversation and more. Less context switching, more efficiency.
  • Dial up the compute: turn the knob to adjust the reasoning level on the fly. Keep things speedy for simple jobs, or crank it up for tasks that need deep thinking.
